# Report layer components

# ReportExample

A complete report built only from the report layer: the shape every Claude Code report should follow. It is a shortened version of the Lynx memory research report.

**Use** it as the template. A report is one page: `body.lr-report` > `.lr-shell` > `aside.lr-nav` (ReportToc) + `main.lr-main`. The first `section.lr-section` opens with the ReportHeader, then Stats and Findings; later sections each start with `.lr-section-head` and hold SubjectCards, ReportTables, ExpandableLists, BudgetStacks, Steps, Timelines, Callouts and Figures; the last section is the SourceList, followed by `footer.lr-footer`.

**Loads** — `tokens.css`, then `reports.css`, then (optional) `reports.js` at the end of the body. In Report Hub these come from `/_ds/lynx-reports/v1/`. No React, no bundle.

**Order of a report**

1. ReportHeader: kind badge, title, the answer in the lead.
2. Two to four Stats, then the main Findings.
3. The evidence, one section per question.
4. What to do next: Steps or a decision Callout.
5. SourceList and footer.

- Do lead with the answer; a reader who stops after the header should have it.
- Don't add sections the question didn't ask for.

---

# ReportHeader

The top of every report: an eyebrow with the kind badge and scope, the title, a lead that states the answer, and a meta line.

**Use** once per report, first in `lr-main`. The lead is the conclusion in one or two sentences, never "This report covers…".

**Markup** — `<header class="lr-header">` holding `.lr-eyebrow` (a KindBadge plus a short scope line), `h1.lr-title`, `p.lr-lead`, and an optional `.lr-meta` row of spans (project › stream, date, version, commit) that the dot separators join.

**Look** — title 24/30 on phones, 30/36 from 560px, semibold, −0.025em; lead 15/26 `muted-foreground`, max 720px; eyebrow and meta in caption and meta sizes.

- Do state the finding with its number in the lead.
- Don't repeat the kind in the title; the badge carries it.

---

# ReportToc

The report's sidebar: the project mark, the sections, and a foot with the date and a theme switch. Sticky beside the content from 1000px; above it, wrapping, on phones.

**Use** `aside.lr-nav` as the first child of `.lr-shell`, holding three panels: `.lr-brand` (a LiveAvatar, `.lr-brand-name` = the project, `.lr-brand-sub` = the report's short name), `nav > ul.lr-toc` of `a.lr-toc-link` (a 16px icon and the section name, `href="#section-id"`), and `.lr-nav-foot` (the date and a `button.lr-icon-btn[data-lr-theme-toggle]` with `.lr-moon` and `.lr-sun` icons). Add `lynx-bloom` to links and `lynx-halo` to the button for Lynx's hover glows.

**Behaviour** — with `reports.js`, the link for the section in view gets `data-active` (an `agent-soft` fill, icon in `agent`), and the button switches and remembers the theme, unless Report Hub has set it.

- Do keep section names to two or three words.
- Don't add a ToC to a report with fewer than three sections; use `lr-shell-single`.

---

# KindBadge

The pill that names a report's kind, in that kind's hue. It leads the eyebrow of every ReportHeader and every row in Report Hub's indexes.

**Use** `<span class="lr-badge" data-kind="<kind>">Kind</span>` with one of the 13 kinds; the word is always written out, sentence case.

| kind | hue | kind | hue |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| investigation | sapphire | experiment | pink |
| incident | red | research | lavender |
| review | mauve | explainer | green |
| audit | peach | runbook | maroon |
| architecture | blue | summary | flamingo |
| plan | teal | benchmark | yellow |
| analysis | sky | | |

**Look** — the hue fills the dot and tints the pill (10% fill, 38% edge); the word stays `foreground`, so every kind reads at full contrast in every palette.

- Do keep the word: several palettes reuse a hue across slots, so colour alone never identifies a kind.
- Don't invent kinds; the list is fixed in Report Hub's config.

---

# ReportBadge

A small pill with a coloured dot for a verdict, status or severity inside a report: "Borrow ideas", "Skip", "Blocker".

**Use** `<span class="lr-badge" data-tone="…">` in table cells, subject cards and findings. Tones: none (neutral, for "skip" or "n/a"), `accent`, `green`, `blue`, `peach`, `red`, `yellow`. `lr-badge-plain` drops the dot for plain tags; wrap tags in `.lr-tags` so they wrap.

**Look** — `radius-full`, caption type, 2px × 10px padding; a 6px dot in the tone; 10% tint and 38% edge of the tone; words in `foreground` (neutral stays `muted-foreground`).

- Do keep each verdict word mapped to one tone across a report (say, accent = borrow, green = adopt).
- Don't make badges clickable.

---

# Stat

A headline number with what it measures and where it came from. Two to four sit in a row under the ReportHeader.

**Use** `.lr-panel.lr-stat` with `.lr-stat-value`, `.lr-stat-label` (a phrase that reads on from the number) and `.lr-stat-src`. Add `.lr-delta` with `data-trend="good" | "bad"` beside the value for a change against a baseline. Lay them out in `.lr-grid.lr-grid-4` (one column on phones, two from 560px, four from 1000px).

**Look** — value 26/32 semibold, tabular figures; label caption `muted-foreground`; source 10px at 70%, pinned to the bottom so a row lines up.

- Do give every number its source.
- Don't show more than four; put the rest in a table.

---

# Finding

A numbered point: a conclusion, a change to make, or an issue found. The default unit of a report's argument.

**Use** `.lr-panel.lr-finding` with `.lr-num`, then an `h3` (the point, as a sentence) and a `p` (why, in one or two sentences). For audits and reviews, wrap the heading in `.lr-finding-head` with a ReportBadge for severity. Lay several out in `.lr-grid.lr-grid-2`.

**Look** — `space-4` padding; the 24px number is an `agent-soft` circle with an `agent-border` edge and `glow-agent`; heading 14/20 medium; body 14/20 `muted-foreground`.

- Do number findings in reading order and refer to them by number elsewhere.
- Don't put more than one point in a finding.

---

# SubjectCard

One thing under evaluation (a library, a vendor, an approach, a file) with its verdict, the evidence, and what to take from it.

**Use** in research, audits and comparisons, one card per subject. `article.lr-panel.lr-subject` holds `.lr-subject-top` (an `h3`, a `.lr-subject-meta` line, and a ReportBadge verdict on the right), then any content (a ReportTable, `.lr-cols` with `.lr-label` headings), and last a `.lr-takeaway`.

**Takeaway** — `.lr-takeaway` is the conclusion for the reader's project: `agent-soft` fill, `agent-border` edge, `radius-xl`, its `.lr-label` in `agent`. One per card, always last.

**Look** — padding `space-4` on phones, `space-6` from 560px; title 18/28 semibold; columns stack under 1000px.

- Do keep the verdict to two or three words.
- Don't put a takeaway anywhere but the end of its card.

---

# ReportTable

A data table for comparing items across attributes, always inside a horizontal scroller so a phone never scrolls the page sideways.

**Use** `.lr-table-wrap` around `table.lr-table`, usually inside `.lr-panel.lr-card`. The first column names the row (medium weight); `lr-table-plain` makes it regular. Right-align numbers with `lr-num-cell` on both the `th` and the `td`. ReportBadges work in cells.

**Look** — 14/20 body; headers 12px medium `muted-foreground`, no wrap; hairlines at 50% (80% under the header); rows tint `agent-soft` on hover.

- Do sort rows by what the reader scans for.
- Don't put paragraphs in cells; move them to an ExpandableList.

---

# ExpandableList

A numbered list of rules, decisions or findings where each heading opens to its evidence. Built on native `<details>`, so it needs no script and prints fully expanded.

**Use** `.lr-panel.lr-items` holding `details.lr-item` elements: a `summary` with a `.lr-num` and the point as a sentence, then `.lr-item-body` with the explanation and a `.lr-src` line for the evidence. Open the first item (`open`) so the pattern is obvious.

**Look** — rows split by 50% hairlines; summary 14/20 medium with a chevron that turns 180° on `ease-spring`; body indented to the text, 14/20 `muted-foreground`.

- Do write every summary so the list reads as a whole when collapsed.
- Don't nest lists inside a body.

---

# BudgetStack

An ordered stack of layers, each with a share bar: what goes into a budget (a prompt, a bundle, a request) and how much each part takes.

**Use** `.lr-stack` (role list) of `.lr-layer` rows: a `.lr-num`, a name block (`.lr-layer-name`, `.lr-layer-sub`), and a bar block (`.lr-bar` with an inner `span` whose width is the share, plus `.lr-bar-label`). `.lr-divider` puts a dashed, labelled line between layers; `data-volatile` marks a layer that changes often (dashed peach edge and bar).

**Look** — `radius-xl` rows at 70% card; 6px bars in `agent`; on phones the bar drops under the name.

- Do set every bar against the same maximum so lengths compare.
- Don't use it for data over time; that is a chart.

---

# Steps

An ordered path: a build order, a rollout, a runbook procedure. Numbered markers joined by a rail.

**Use** `ol.lr-steps` of `li.lr-step`, each a `.lr-num` then a block with an `h3` (the step, verb first) and a `p`. Add `data-done` to tick a finished step (the number becomes a check on an `agent` fill). Usually inside `.lr-panel.lr-card`.

**Look** — 24px markers, a 1px `agent-border` rail between them, `space-5` between steps; body 14/20 `muted-foreground`.

- Do keep steps in the order they must happen; for options use Findings.
- Don't hide a step's command in prose; put it in a CodeBlock under the step.

---

# Timeline

Dated events in order: an incident from alert to resolution, or the history of a stream.

**Use** `ol.lr-timeline` of `li.lr-event`, each holding a block with `.lr-event-time`, an `h3` and a `p`. `data-tone` colours the event's dot: `red` (impact starts), `peach` (finding), `green` (resolved), `accent` (decision); none is neutral.

**Look** — a 10px dot with a soft halo in its tone, joined by a hairline; time in meta size, tabular figures.

- Do give times in one zone and say which on the first event.
- Don't colour every event; keep tone for the turning points.

---

# Callout

One aside the reader shouldn't miss: a note, a warning, a recorded decision, a success or a danger.

**Use** `.lr-callout` with a 16px Lucide icon (`svg.lr-icon`) then a `p`, or a block whose first `strong` is a short heading. `data-tone`: none (note, blue), `warning` (peach), `decision` (accent), `success` (green), `danger` (red).

**Look** — `radius-2xl`, `space-4` padding, 7% tint and 25% edge of the tone; the icon takes the tone; text 14/20 `foreground`.

- Do keep a callout to one or two sentences.
- Don't stack callouts; one per section at most.

---

# Verdict

The outcome of a review, stated once, right after the ReportHeader: approve, request changes, or reject.

**Use** `.lr-verdict` with `data-verdict="approve" | "changes" | "reject"`, a `.lr-verdict-mark` holding a check, alert or x icon, then `.lr-verdict-word` and a `p` saying what it rests on (refer to findings by number).

**Look** — `radius-2xl`, 8% tint and 40% edge of the verdict's hue (green, peach, red); a 36px filled circle mark; the word at 18/28 semibold.

- Do say exactly what blocks merging.
- Don't use it outside reviews; for a recommendation use a decision Callout.

---

# CodeBlock

Code in a report: a file excerpt, a command, a diff. Scrolls sideways instead of wrapping.

**Use** `figure.lr-code` with an optional `figcaption` (the file path or what the snippet is), then `pre > code`. For a diff, put each changed line in `span.lr-add` or `span.lr-del` (shown with + and −). With `reports.js` loaded, a Copy button appears in the caption; it copies the code as it reads after the change, leaving removed lines out.

**Look** — `radius-xl`, a muted ground, 12.5/20 mono; added lines tinted green, removed lines red.

- Do keep excerpts short and link the full file by commit.
- Don't paste secrets; the publisher warns, but the reader still sees them.

---

# Figure

An image, screenshot or diagram with a caption that states what it shows and a line for where it came from.

**Use** `figure.lr-figure` holding an `img` or inline `svg` (give a diagram `role="img"` and an `aria-label` that states what it shows), then a `figcaption` with the point and a `.lr-src` span for the source. Images live in the report's `assets/` folder.

**Look** — media fills the width up to its own size, `radius-xl`; caption 12/16 `muted-foreground`, source in meta size.

- Do draw diagrams with token colours (`var(--border)`, `var(--agent)`, `var(--foreground)`) so they follow the theme.
- Do use Chart, BarList, ShareBar or Sparkline for data; Figure is for pictures, not numbers.
- Don't use a screenshot of text; set the text.

---

# SourceList

The sources a report drew on, grouped under short headings, ending every report that cites anything. With it, the report footer.

**Use** `.lr-panel.lr-card.lr-sources` with `h3` group headings and `ul` lists of links; related links can share a line with ` · `. Close the report with `p.lr-footer` (or `footer.lr-footer`) for caveats about the sources.

**Look** — one column on phones, two from 1000px; groups never split across columns; links 14/20 in `agent`.

- Do link the exact page used, not a homepage.
- Don't list sources the report didn't use.
